text:
tomas.devex: Heads up — ran into confusing behavior in the sample-apps workshop. CLI sets project in ~/.redwood/config but node SDK prefers REDWOOD_PROJECT env var. New users end up with mismatched project scope.

lina.sdk: thanks for flagging. we did that because CLI config was easier for interactive setups. what do we want the canonical source of truth to be? env var, config file, or token-scoped project?

omar.security: from a least-surprise + audit perspective: token-scoped project > explicit env/config > defaults. Tokens that carry project/org claims are authoritative. SDKs should validate that provided REDWOOD_API_KEY matches REDWOOD_PROJECT if both present and warn on mismatch.

sam.ops: agree on validation. operationally, env vars are easiest for containers; config files are more helpful for local dev. we should document precedence and provide helper to normalize. also: many teams still use REDWOOD_TOKEN or REDWOOD_KEY – need a deprecation path.

tomas.devex: proposal: canonical names are REDWOOD_API_KEY, REDWOOD_ORG, REDWOOD_PROJECT. fallback aliases allowed for 2 minor releases with a deprecation log. CLI should migrate .env.example and config writer to use canonical names.

lina.sdk: implementation note: we'll implement fallback in this order inside SDKs: constructor arg > env var > CLI config file > credentials file > metadata service. and include a small validation step that tries to detect conflicting scopes and surfaces a clear error.

omar.security: rotation behavior: for short-lived creds we must support refreshing transparently. SDKs should expose a pluggable refresh callback and default to: on 401 -> reload credentials once -> retry single request -> if still 401, run onAuthFailure hook and surface error. document that SDKs do not retry infinitely.

sam.ops: addendum — to avoid thundering herd during rotation, default retry should include randomized jitter and exponential backoff when multiple clients hit 401 in same window. also expose configuration for retry-window and backoff params.

lina.sdk: we'll add onAuthFailure(cb) and options.retryPolicy to SDKs. default policy: maxAttempts=2, baseDelay=200ms, jitter=100ms. can be overridden by advanced users.

tomas.devex: can we add a small migration helper script in devex/tools that scans repo/.env and offers to rename REDWOOD_TOKEN -> REDWOOD_API_KEY and migrate REDWOOD_PROJECT from .redwood/config? opt-in only and prints audit log.

omar.security: that's fine if script prints security guidance and warns about committing creds. also add a test that validates SDKs emit deprecation warnings when aliases are used.

cred-rot-bot: scheduled audit: teams with tokens older than 60 days will receive an email next Monday. :alarm_clock:

lina.sdk: i'll open PRs for node + python SDKs: add canonical env handling, deprecation warnings, onAuthFailure hook, and a small docs snippet showing precedence + rotation example.

sam.ops: i'll update CLI writer to prefer canonical vars and add a --migrate-env flag to automatically produce a migrated .env (no secrets written, only var names).

tomas.devex: great. last request: include a short sample in READMEs for "best practice": prefer token-scoped projects, otherwise set REDWOOD_PROJECT or pass project explicitly. eg:

```
# recommended env vars for container deployments
export REDWOOD_API_KEY=sk_live_xxx
export REDWOOD_PROJECT=payment-service
```

and an SDK snippet:

```js
// fallback + validation
const apiKey = opts.apiKey || process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY || readCliConfig().apiKey;
const project = opts.project || process.env.REDWOOD_PROJECT || readCliConfig().project;
if (tokenHasClaims(apiKey) && tokenProjectClaim(apiKey) !== project) {
  console.warn('token project claim does not match REDWOOD_PROJECT');
}
const client = new Redwood({ apiKey, project });
```

lina.sdk: sounds good. assigning myself for SDK changes and will add deprecation timeline in PR body.

tomas.devex: thanks everyone — moving action items to the devex board and creating a small checklist for docs/migration/SDK/CLI/security. closing thread unless blockers pop up. :white_check_mark:
